$comment: The PR gate's pinned baseline, not only a quarantine: the suites jest.gate.config.js does not run, plus the numbers .github/ci/jest-gate-check.mjs holds the gate to. REMOVALS ONLY for 'suites': the checker fails any PR that adds a path not present on the base branch, so an addition needs SA review and a visible override. Every entry was red on main at 'since'. The floors are raised by hand and never lowered without SA. Pinned 2026-10-04 from PR #210's first Linux run (813 suites / 15,813 tests), about 2% below it: a bulk-deletion backstop, not an exact count (G1 and G5 are exact). Workplan: docs/workplans/TEST_STRATEGY_AND_CI_TIERING_WORKPLAN.md section 0.
$refusalsComment: G8's ceiling on how many network connections the gate refuses (tests/jest-no-network.ts records them; a unit test must not reach the network). Note the SIGN: minSuites/minTests are floors that may only RISE, maxRefusedConnections is a ceiling that may only FALL, and the checker hard-FAILS a raise or a removal rather than noting it, because editing it up is exactly how a new leak would get waved through. NOT PINNED YET: the count can only be measured honestly where CI runs the gate (on Windows ~29 suites fail early on CRLF-sensitive source scans and never reach their leaking code), so G8 is report-only until a real CI run supplies the number. When pinning it, record here: the date, the commit, how many runs it was the maximum of, and the flake margin with its reasoning — a floating promise's socket may never open if its worker exits first, so the count is not perfectly deterministic. The margin is a flake buffer, not a licence.
